T: Ring the bells. Ring the dinner bell.
D: A kind bell-ringer hidden in Notre Dame sneaks out to the Festival of Fools in Paris.
P: Serve the snacks when Quasimodo sneaks down to the Festival of Fools.
S: the Festival of Fools in the square
Thin crêpe batter rested an hour, cooked in a buttered pan, folded with ham and gruyère, or with sugar and lemon.
Victor, Hugo and Laverne, the gargoyles
Choux pastry with gruyère piped into small balls, baked at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed and hollow.
the busy Paris market below the cathedral
Baguette slices toasted with olive oil, topped with brie and fig jam, or with tomato and basil.
M: Beef chuck browned and simmered 3 hours in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions, served with buttery mash.
Chicken thighs braised with white wine, garlic, olives and herbs until tender, with crusty bread.
W: the great cathedral of Notre Dame
Madeleine batter of butter, eggs, sugar and lemon zest rested an hour, baked in shell tins at 200C for 10 minutes.
K: a red syrup drink from the Paris streets
French-style sirop à l'eau: grenadine poured into iced soda water so it settles red at the bottom.

s.note: the Festival of Fools in the square
s.how: Whisk 150g flour, 2 eggs and 375ml milk and rest an hour. Cook thin crepes in a buttered pan. Fill half with ham and gruyere and fold, warming until melted. Sprinkle the rest with sugar and lemon juice and fold into quarters.

s.note: the busy Paris market below the cathedral
s.how: Slice a baguette, brush with olive oil and toast. Top half with brie and a spoon of fig jam. Top the rest with chopped tomato, torn basil and salt. Lay them out like a stall at the Paris market below the bell tower.

m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck and 150g bacon. Add 250g mushrooms and 200g peeled pickling onions and cook until golden. Pour in a bottle of red wine and simmer for 3 hours. Serve over buttery mash from 1kg potatoes.

w.note: the great cathedral of Notre Dame
w.how: Melt 100g butter and cool. Whisk 2 eggs with 100g sugar and lemon zest until thick, then fold in 100g flour and the butter. Rest for an hour. Spoon into greased shell tins and bake at 200C for 10 minutes. Dust with icing sugar.

d.note: a red syrup drink from the Paris streets
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice. Pour 30ml grenadine into each, top slowly with 200ml soda water and let it sit in a red layer at the bottom until stirred.
